_comment: The subsystem tags this emulator's operational log lines are allowed to carry, the
call sites recorded as exempt from carrying one, the pre-FABRIC_* names of log knobs
that are still read, and the log lines excused from the credential-redaction rule.
`subsystems` is DERIVED and written by scripts/check_logging_quality.py --update;
`exemptions`, `legacyEnvNames` and `redactionExemptions` are HAND-WRITTEN and are
preserved across --update.
THE MEASURED BASELINE when this landed: 30 `log.*` call sites across 12 non-test Go
files, in a tree of 212 non-test Go sources. Exactly ONE test in the whole tree
asserted a log line (internal/api/livy_catalog_test.go, via log.SetOutput). Four
delimiter conventions for the subsystem tag coexisted -- bracketed
(`[onelake-dfs]`), colon (`livy:`), space-delimited (`notebook drive job=`) and no
tag at all -- so no single grep could select one subsystem's lines out of a compose
log. docs/64-logging-quality.md carries the findings table with file:line evidence.
ROUND 2's BASELINE, re-measured from a clean checkout before anything changed: 35
call sites across 13 non-test files naming 14 subsystems, in a tree of 224 non-test
Go sources (563 total), with 4 test files now asserting a log line. And the finding
round 1 did not measure: 214 non-test call sites write a 500 and 268 write some 5xx,
across 47 files and seven error writers (writeErr alone is 150) -- and not one of
them logged anything. All 35 existing lines belonged to background drivers, traces
and lifecycle paths, so the single status that always means "the emulator is broken,
rather than the request" was the one class of failure with no server-side record.
The detail was not lost, it went the wrong way: writeErr echoes err.Error() into the
response body, so the CLIENT learned what happened and the operator reading the
compose log learned nothing. internal/server/fault.go closes that at the root.
WHY `fault` NAMES AN EVENT CLASS RATHER THAN A COMPONENT, which every other tag in
this list does. A 5xx observed at the root has not yet been attributed to a
subsystem -- that is the same argument the main.go exemption below already makes
about log.Fatal, and the same one internal/server/server.go's boundBodies makes about
answering 413 in the control plane's error shape: "a request refused before routing
has not yet been attributed to a surface". Attributing the fault would mean either
editing the 214 sites or guessing from the path, and a guessed tag is worse than an
honest one, because `grep 'fault: '` would then select an incomplete set while
looking complete.
THE FAILURE SHAPE is the one this repository has written down twice already, in
python/tests/test_make_check_runs_in_ci.py's words: a check that passes is
indistinguishable from a check that is running. A log line is the same thing turned
inside out. These lines are the only account the emulator gives of its own failure
paths -- a Livy session whose lakehouse did not mount, a notebook driver that
panicked, a recording file that could not be opened -- and nothing registered which
subsystems log at all. A handler that stops logging its failure path is then
indistinguishable from a handler that has no failures: silence where the signal
would be, with no diff to notice.
The gate is asymmetric in the same direction as docs/compat-surface.json. A tag in
the tree and not here is a STALE LEDGER: run --update and let the diff be the review
of what vocabulary the log now speaks. An entry here and not in the tree fails until
someone deletes it -- a tag nobody emits goes on blessing a spelling, an exemption
whose call site is gone goes on excusing a file, and a redaction exemption whose
call site is gone goes on excusing a credential in a diagnostic.
IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER A LINE IS TRUE, or about whether the right things are
logged at all, and it still does not record SEVERITY -- docs/64-logging-quality.md's
F3, deferred twice now, with the argument restated there. It holds the shape: a tag
a reader can grep for, no library that exits the process out from under its caller,
a log knob the surface ledger can see, and no log argument that reaches a credential
without passing through a redactor.

exemptions.reason: The whole message IS the error, and there is no subsystem to attribute it to: this is main() refusing to start, before any subsystem exists to have failed. run() has already composed the context into the error -- a bad flag, an unopenable data directory, a port already in use -- and prefixing that with a tag would name the process rather than a component of it. It is also the one site where log.Fatal is correct, which R2 permits here and nowhere else: cmd/ IS the process, so exiting is its decision to make.

legacyEnvNames.name: ONELAKE_TRACE
legacyEnvNames.reason: The pre-FABRIC_* spelling of the OneLake request trace, shipped in released binaries and still honoured so an existing shell export or compose override keeps working. It is also the reason this audit found anything at all: because it is not named FABRIC_*, check_backward_compat.py's env literal pattern matches only FABRIC_[A-Z0-9_]+ and could not see it, so it appeared in no docs/, in no envVars list, and in no docsUndocumented reason -- unlike its sibling FABRIC_TDS_TRACE, which carries both. A knob outside the surface ledger can be renamed or deleted with every gate in this repository staying green. To be retired in a release whose notes say so; until then this entry is what keeps the guard from reporting a knob somebody is deliberately still honouring.
